name: Kolanut Crown Capital
tagline: From one desk in the market to ringing the bell for Africa's big deals

ownerCharacter.name: Madam Ronke Adigun
ownerCharacter.look: Woman, 38, medium build, low-cut natural hair, emerald green skirt suit with gold ankara lapels, flat shoes, reading glasses on a chain, fat red deal folder.
ownerCharacter.backstory: Daughter of a pepper seller, she kept her mother's sales book from age 12. After ten years as a junior accountant she set a plastic desk beside the market gate to help traders register and raise money properly.

storyline.title: One Desk, One Umbrella
storyline.stage: A plastic desk, a stamp and a borrowed laptop under an umbrella at the market gate
storyline.story: Traders want loans and partners but have no papers. Ronke registers their businesses and writes their first simple accounts. If the first ten clients are not happy, the desk goes back to the landlord.
storyline.unlock: Client bench, first analyst desk and the Business Starter Pack line

storyline.title: The First Fund Raise
storyline.stage: A one-room office above a fabric shop with two desks and a noisy fan
storyline.story: Mama Sikira's cold room needs N100 million. Ronke must write a clean investment memo and find honest investors. One wrong number in the memo and nobody will trust her name again.
storyline.unlock: Private Fund Raise line, an associate, and the success fee rule

storyline.title: Boutique on the Island
storyline.stage: A small glass-fronted advisory office on Lagos Island with a proper client lounge
storyline.story: Bigger clients arrive: a bakery chain, a bus company. To be taken seriously, the firm needs a licence from the securities regulator and N2 billion in capital. Partners must be found.
storyline.unlock: Adviser licence, compliance desk and a pool car for client visits

storyline.title: Ring the Bell
storyline.stage: Two floors with a deal room, a printing corner and a wall clock for each market
storyline.story: A family noodle maker wants to list on the exchange. The prospectus must pass the regulator, the roadshow must fill the order book, and listing day cannot slip. The whole market is watching.
storyline.unlock: IPO Prospectus line, roadshow travel and the order book mini-game

storyline.title: Bonds for the Bridge
storyline.stage: A full floor in a Lagos tower with a bond desk and a visiting room for officials
storyline.story: A state needs N20 billion for a bridge and a water plant. Ronke flies to Abuja for approvals and proves every naira will be tracked. A late coupon would hurt pensioners, so the plan must hold.
storyline.unlock: Bond Issue line, Abuja office and the underwriting licence at N7 billion capital

storyline.title: Two Become One
storyline.stage: A tower headquarters with a locked data room and a quiet floor for secret deals
storyline.story: Two rival cement makers want to merge. Both sides fear being cheated. Ronke must value each fairly, keep the deal secret until announced, and win approval from the competition regulator.
storyline.unlock: Merger Deal line, the secure data room and the wall between teams

storyline.title: Money That Works
storyline.stage: Headquarters plus an asset management floor serving pensions and cooperatives
storyline.story: Old clients now ask her to look after their savings. Teachers' cooperatives and pension funds join. Growing it slowly and safely matters more than showing off, because this is people's retirement.
storyline.unlock: Asset management fees, the London office and international flights

storyline.title: Lagos to New York
storyline.stage: A full investment bank with offices in Lagos, Abuja, London, Dubai and New York
storyline.story: A Nigerian tech company wants to list in Lagos and abroad on the same day. Five offices, three time zones, one bell. If it works, the pepper seller's daughter becomes Africa's dealmaker.
storyline.unlock: Dubai and New York offices, dual listings and the Dealmaker of the Year trophy

howItFitsTheEngine: Clients arrive in the client lounge and drop files: receipts, accounts, budget books, sealed data boxes. The player carries files to analyst desks, where staff turn them into finished deals: a starter pack, a memo, a prospectus, a bond, a merger agreement. The player carries each bound deal to the deal room, where the client signs, shakes hands, pays the fee and rings a small bell.

moneyMechanics.howItWorks: Each deal pays a small retainer at the start (10% of the fee) and the rest only when the deal closes: about 2.5% on small raises, 1.5% on IPOs and mergers, 1% on bonds.
moneyMechanics.realBasis: Advisers are mostly paid a negotiated percentage of the money raised or the deal value, on completion. The game's rates are simplified.

moneyMechanics.howItWorks: IPO and bond lines stay locked until the firm holds N2 billion in capital for the advisory licence. Underwriting unlocks at N7 billion. Capital is kept aside and cannot be spent.
moneyMechanics.realBasis: The securities regulator's 2026 rules set N2bn for advisory-only issuing houses and N7bn for those that underwrite.

moneyMechanics.howItWorks: During an IPO or bond, investor orders fill a bar over 3 game days. Roadshow trips add up to 40%. At 100% or more the full fee is paid; under 100% the fee shrinks in line.
moneyMechanics.realBasis: Big offers use book building: investors bid over a set period and the price or coupon is fixed from the bids.

moneyMechanics.howItWorks: With the N7bn licence, you may promise to buy unsold shares for an extra 1.5% fee. If the book fills only 80%, your capital buys the 20% and is tied up for 10 game days.
moneyMechanics.realBasis: Underwriters guarantee an offer by taking up securities investors do not buy, for a commission.

moneyMechanics.howItWorks: The asset management floor earns 1.5% a year on money looked after, paid monthly. N10 billion under care pays about N12.5 million a month, deal or no deal.
moneyMechanics.realBasis: Fund managers charge a yearly percentage of assets under management, giving steady income between deals.

moneyMechanics.howItWorks: Each December, staff expect a bonus of 30% to 150% of yearly pay, scaled to deals closed. Pay it and speed rises 10% next year; skip it and your best analyst may leave.
moneyMechanics.realBasis: Investment banking pay in Nigeria is base salary plus a performance bonus that can exceed the base.

travel.why: Sit with a state finance team to plan a bond for roads and water, and inspect the project sites
Meet the securities regulator on licences and approvals, and open the Abuja office for state clients
Roadshow to pension funds and diaspora investors, and open the London office for cross-border deals
Meet Gulf funds looking for African deals, and close mergers with trading groups based there
Pitch the big global funds and ring the bell for a dual listing; the last office to open

rivalsAndAllies.line: Small madam, IPO no be pepper soup. Leave am for big boys.

rivalsAndAllies.name: Prof. Ngozi Umeh
rivalsAndAllies.line: A deal you cannot explain to your mother is a deal you should not sign.

rivalsAndAllies.name: Director Halima Sule
rivalsAndAllies.line: Page 47 does not match page 12. Fix it, then we can talk approval.

rivalsAndAllies.name: Mama Sikira
rivalsAndAllies.line: Ronke, you chop today? Deal fit wait, stomach no fit.

events.name: Oversubscribed!
events.text: Investors want twice the shares on offer. Order book bonus for today's deals.

events.name: Regulator's Query
events.text: The regulator sends back a prospectus with ten questions. That desk pauses to fix it.

events.name: Market Wobble
events.text: Share prices dip and investors turn shy. Order books fill slower today.

events.name: Referral From Mama
events.text: Mama Sikira sends five traders with their shoeboxes. Extra starter pack clients.

events.name: Leak Scare
events.text: Someone left a merger file on the printer. Lock it up fast or the client loses trust.

events.name: Deal of the Year
events.text: A finance magazine names your bond Deal of the Year. More clients in the lounge.

events.name: Generator Wahala
events.text: Power cuts out at deadline. Desks slow down until the generator kicks in.

events.name: Rates Come Down
events.text: Interest rates ease. States and companies rush to issue bonds. Bond fees up today.

endgame: Kolanut Crown Capital runs five offices from Lagos to New York, leads Africa's biggest listings, bonds and mergers, looks after N1 trillion in savings, and funds a free business clinic at the market gate where it all began.
risksToHandleCarefully: Never reward insider dealing, kickbacks or cooked numbers; show them only as mistakes to stop. State clients are unnamed and non-partisan. The order book must not feel like gambling. Make clear in-game money and returns are not real.

research.claim: Nigeria's securities regulator raised minimum capital in January 2026 to N7 billion for issuing houses that underwrite and N2 billion for advisory-only issuing houses, with a June 30, 2027 deadline.
Investment banking base pay in Nigeria runs about N250,000 to N600,000 a month for analysts and N500,000 to N1.2 million for associates, with bonuses of roughly 30% to 150% on top.

A 2026 Lagos State 10-year bond of up to N200 billion was priced by book building at an indicative 16.50% to 16.75%, with a N5 million minimum subscription and a sinking fund fed by a standing payment order.
A N42 billion public share offer in January 2026 used one lead issuing house, seven joint issuing houses and a registrar, and stayed open to investors for about two weeks.
Fund managers overseeing more than N20 billion now need N5 billion in capital, and mid-tier managers need N2 billion.
